# Datamosh

The look of a video with its keyframes removed: motion drags the old picture along in blocks, smearing it into the new one until the next keyframe resets it. Motion comes from the velocity buffer or from a light optical flow of the image.

<EffectDemo effect="datamosh" />

## Usage

```ts
import { EffectComposer } from '@mk7s/xtree/core';
import { datamosh } from '@mk7s/xtree/effects/datamosh';

const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer);
composer.setScene(scene, camera);
composer.add(datamosh({ preset: 'melt' }));
// Animated effects hold still until play() (or { autoplay: true }).
composer.play();
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => composer.render());
```

Every parameter is also a property: `effect.source = 'flow'`. Uniform changes take effect on the next frame without recompiling; parameters marked _structural_ recompile the pass that contains the effect.

## Parameters

| Parameter               | Type                 | Default  | Range      | Description                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | -------------------- | -------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source` _(structural)_ | 'velocity' \| 'flow' | `'flow'` |            | Where motion comes from: the scene’s velocity buffer, or optical flow estimated from the image (works on video and 2D content too). |
| `blockSize`             | number               | `16`     | 4 – 64 px  | Size of the motion blocks, like video macroblocks.                                                                                  |
| `strength`              | number               | `1.5`    | 0 – 6      | How far each frame’s motion pushes the old picture.                                                                                 |
| `refresh`               | number               | `0.04`   | 0 – 0.5    | How much of the new frame bleeds in each frame; 0 never recovers until a keyframe.                                                  |
| `keyframeInterval`      | number               | `3`      | 0.5 – 20 s | Seconds between keyframes, which restore the clean picture.                                                                         |
| `amount`                | number               | `1`      | 0 – 1      | Mix between the original and the moshed image.                                                                                      |

Every effect also has `blend` (any of the 26 [blend modes](/reference/shaders#modes)), `opacity` (0–1) and `enabled`.

## Presets

| Preset   | Settings                                              |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `melt`   | `strength: 3`, `refresh: 0.01`, `keyframeInterval: 6` |
| `blocky` | `blockSize: 32`, `strength: 2`                        |
| `subtle` | `strength: 0.8`, `refresh: 0.1`                       |
| `scene`  | `source: 'velocity'`, `strength: 2`                   |

Apply one with `datamosh({ preset: 'name' })` or `effect.applyPreset('name')`; presets start from the defaults.

## Details

- **Family:** Glitch & signal · tracked as story X6.5 in the [plan](https://github.com/s4njee/xtree/blob/main/plan.md).
- **Passes:** samples the pass input at other positions, so it starts a new merged pass; following pixel effects join that pass. It also renders its own intermediate passes before the merged pass.
- **Geometry buffers:** depend on its settings; with the defaults it reads none.
- **Masks:** set `effect.mask` to a texture, depth range or selection to limit where it applies; see [masks](/guide/masks).
- **Motion:** Freezes: when motion is off (reduced motion, high contrast or `composer.motion = false`) the effect holds its current frame.
- **Size:** 7.3 KB gzip budget for `@mk7s/xtree/effects/datamosh`, including the shared effect runtime.

## Credits

Original implementation (MIT). References: Lucas and Kanade, An iterative image registration technique, 1981 (block optical flow); Datamoshing by dropping I-frames, as described by video artists.

## Related

- [Pixel sort](./pixel-sort) — Sorts runs of pixels by brightness or hue along rows or columns, the glitch-art streaks of pixel sorting.
- [JPEG artifacts](./jpeg) — Compresses each frame the way JPEG does (8×8 DCT blocks quantized with the standard tables, color at quarter resolution) and decodes it again, for blocky, ringing, smeared-color artifacts at low quality.
- [Motion blur](./motion-blur) — Blurs moving objects and camera motion along their path, as a camera shutter does.
